replication.target_description: Study 2, omnibus one-way ANOVA of anagram persistence time across Suppress, Express and no-additional-instructions groups. This is not a no-emotional-control condition-specific test.

n.quote: 76 undergraduates (68 females and 8 males) enrolled in a college in the northeastern U.S. volunteered to participate in this study. A one-way analysis of variance revealed no statistically significant differences in anagram time among the three groups, F (2,73) = .274, p = .761.
n.sample_role: Participants in the three-group anagram-time ANOVA; reported participant count is consistent with its residual degrees of freedom.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this ANOVA.

es.quote: A one-way analysis of variance revealed no statistically significant differences in anagram time among the three groups, F (2,73) = .274, p = .761.

p.quote: A one-way analysis of variance revealed no statistically significant differences in anagram time among the three groups, F (2,73) = .274, p = .761.

reported_success.quote: Our failure to replicate the findings of prior studies was unexpected, and is puzzling.

notes: Original: condition labels and PDF p. 5 identify Study 1, whereas input study_o is 2; target_match is false. Extracted the within-condition pretest–posttest test, which is the condition-specific test printed there; the page also reports between-condition contrasts. Original PDF was visually checked to resolve OCR t/r errors. Replication: supplied emotional-control description does not match Study 2 thought-control manipulation, so target_match is false. Authors’ failed-replication verdict is study-level, not a verdict about an emotional-control condition. Original p is printed only as ns; no numerical p bound inferred. Replication F and p are an omnibus result, not a control-condition simple test.
